description.narrative:
The overall objective of the intervention is to contribute to peacebuilding in Colombia through the reintegration of FARC ex-combatants and their full exercise of citizenship and related rights in conditions of equality.
The intervention will contribute specifically to the establishment and development of ECOMUN, the cooperative organisation of ex-FARC combatants, as a vehicle for transformation and for the creation of conditions and mechanisms for effective reincorporation of ex-combatant men and women within the framework of a social, solidarity and environmentally sustainable economy.
Expected results by the end of the intervention are:
Result 1: ECOMUN is strengthened as a democratic cooperative organisation under the principles of the solidarity economy for the effective participation of ex-combatant women and men and the communities surrounding the reincorporation areas, within the framework of the peace agreements implementation.
Result 2: ECOMUNs grassroots, ex-combatant women and men and the communities surrounding the reincorporation areas have identified concrete initiatives for community reincorporation and collaboration in social and economic life at the local level.

Detta är ett projektstöd för organisations- och kapacitetsutveckling av ECOMUN och lokala kooperativ för demobiliserade FARC-medlemmar, genom den svenska civilsamhällesorganisationen We Effect.
Insatsen ämnar att bidra till genomförandet av fredsavtalet mellan Colombias regering och FARC och därmed till en varaktig fred med mänsklig säkerhet, genom att förbättra förutsättningarna för den socioekonomiska återintegreringen av före detta gerillasoldater i samhället, med fokus på socialt och miljömässigt hållbar produktiv sysselsättning och jämställdhetsintegrering. ECOMUN är den organisation som FARC föreslagit i syfte att stödja och stärka de lokala kooperativ som bildats av före detta soldater. Projektet har utvecklats tillsammans med ECOMUN och We Effect tillhandahåller resurser och specialiserad rådgivning för bildandet av organisationen, liksom dess möjligheter att verka och utvecklas till en ledande organisation för den kollektiva återintegreringsprocessen, i linje med de före detta soldaternas egna behov och önskemål. Ingen vidareförmedling av medel sker till ECOMUN eller de lokala kooperativen.

This is a project support for organizational and capacity development of ECOMUN and local cooperatives for demobilized FARC members, through the Swedish civil society organization We Effect.
The effort aims to contribute to the implementation of the peace agreement between the Government of Colombia and the FARC and thus to a lasting peace with human security, by improving the conditions for the socio-economic reincorporation of former guerrilla soldiers into society, focusing on socially and environmentally sustainable productive activities and gender integration. ECOMUN is the organization proposed by the FARC in order to support and strengthen the local cooperatives formed by their ex-combatants. The project has been developed together with ECOMUN and We Effect provides resources and specialized advice for the formalization of the organization, as well as its possibilities to operate and develop into a leading organization for the collective reintegration process, in line with the ex-combatants' own needs and wishes. No transfer of funds takes place to ECOMUN or the local cooperatives.

We Effect (WE) has facilitated the internal democratic process and compliance with Colombian law and constitution of ECOMUN, the regional coordination in the Caribbean region- FEDECARIBE and Southwest region Federation, as well as the 43 grassroot organizations from the Caribbean region, Chocó and Cauca.
In the first component, that aims at strengthening ECOMUN as a democratic cooperative organization under the principles of the solidarity economy, significant progress has been made in the formal constitution of Ecomun and its government structure (Administrative Council and Surveillance board). We Effect (WE) has facilitated the internal democratic process and compliance with Colombian law. WE has provided external consultants in cooperativism and social and solidarity economy, as well as for regional dialogue with grassroot organizations. Capacity building included advice on document management, financial statements, tax regime, registration renewal, contributions to social security system, sources of financing, social control, management, legality control and financial reports.
The final report showed that the participation of women has increased from 26% to 39% by the end of the project and that the five care initiatives promoted by the project, has facilitated additional time for women to participate in the income generating activities and the decision-making processes. The project paid special attention to the training of women in cooperativism and social and solidarity economy through cooperative schools for women. Two schools were held in the Southwest and the Caribbean region that let the theoretical and practical bases with grassroots organizations and reinforced them with a special course on mutualism. Likewise, the capacities of men and women from the organizations were strengthened for the formation and consolidation of gender committees, which are made up of women and men and have the mission of promoting equal rights and obligations without discrimination.
As mentioned before, the psychosocial support has also been positively valued. WE has provided consultants to accompany psychosocial healing. They provided training aimed at improving their emotional and social well-being and developing tools and capacities for conflict transformation. it contributed to the development of tools to manage situations of emotional stress and mitigate traumatic effects caused by violent situations. A complementary consultancy about security and self-protective measures, was also positive to strengthen capacities and enabling spaces for the transformation of conflicts and the coexistence between reincorporated people and communities; to create systems and cultural habits of protection and non-violent self-protection. In addition, organizational awareness about risks management was developed.
As regards the second component that aims to help ECOMUNs grassroots, ex-combatants and the communities identify concrete initiatives for collective Reincorporation, a baseline of initiatives was created: In the Caribbean region the main activities are bovine livestock, oviculture, pig farming, poultry farming, beekeeping, clothing, artisan weaving and the growing of cassava, yam, sesame, and bean crops. In Cauca, cattle raising, pig farming, fish farming, poultry farming and the growing of coffee, chili peppers and tomatoes. In Chocó: health care products made from medicinal plants, community shops, accessories for wood construction. New ideas are agro-ecological tourism and bio-factories with agro-ecological inputs.
Finally, in 2022 the Caribbean mutual association for life and peace (Mutual Vid-Paz is its Spanish acronym) was created with 60% of women as participants and 100% of women in the directive council. The main goal is to promote the financial inclusion and the savings and credit culture.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
